summary: The Pentagon released a new batch of UAP files this week as part of the Trump administration's PURSUE initiative, continuing what advocates say is the most significant government disclosure effort to date. The release included previously classified videos and documents, with The Black Vault simultaneously launching a searchable archive of the materials to make them more accessible to researchers. However, the research community pushed back on the notion that data dumps alone constitute meaningful disclosure, noting that documents without official acknowledgment or explanation of their implications leave the public largely in the dark. A House Republican also requested a private contractor brief lawmakers on UFO-related work, signaling ongoing congressional interest in pulling together the full picture of what government and defense contractors actually know. Separately, newly surfaced NASA documents show the agency has internal protocols for announcing the discovery of extraterrestrial life, though whether any of this week's releases relate to such a threshold remains unclear.
